document.title: Information Memorandum from Richard W. Murphy to Mr. Armacost. Subject: Where We Stand in our Relationship with India
document.authors: Richard W. Murphy, Department of State
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), A New Phase in the Great Game: U.S., Soviets, India, Pakistan vied to shape a new Afghanistan in late 1980s | National Security Archive
document.note: Describes stagnation or deterioration in U.S.-Indian relations after unrealistic expectations following Gandhi's 1985 visit. Blames continued U.S. support for Pakistan and its covert nuclear program. Suggests initiatives such as technology sales and high-level dialogue; Pakistan arms sales listed as a pitfall.

key_claims: US-India relations, improved after Rajiv Gandhi's June 1985 visit, show signs of stagnation by May 1986.
India blames the US for not pressuring Pakistan over its covert nuclear program and alleged support for Sikh terrorists.
US aims to build an Indo-US relationship to balance Indo-Soviet ties and make Indian foreign policy more balanced.
High technology transfer, especially the supercomputer and Light Combat Aircraft, is central to Rajiv's view of the relationship.
The new US aid package and arms sales to Pakistan are expected to give Rajiv's critics ammunition.
US should reassure India on the purpose of security assistance to Pakistan.
